findings.title: The unattended crew Helm's rule assumes a flight branch the Hound layout doesn't have
findings.claim: §3 says that with no Helm attendant, the crew Helm's throttle returns to 0 and the ship coasts, and that 'a held heading still turns it'. §4 says the compressor runs unattended. But today an unattended Helm on a layout without helmHoldsUnattended (the Hound/Cutter) leaves crew.helm false, so stepDuel flies NO_AXES. The ship isn't turned by a held heading at all, and the per-mille ramp-down would never reach flyShip. The spec doesn't say whether a newtonianHelm class now sets crew.helm = true while unattended. It also doesn't say which axes that slot flies: the heading turn, the boost from helmBoost(d, NO_HELD), and crewThrust(thrMille) while it returns to 0. The two mirrors of the sim's rule aren't named either.
findings.evidence: spec L140, L106-L107, L166; step.ts:L279-L287 (only `st.layout.helmHoldsUnattended === true` sets crew.helm and flies a heading turn and throttle; the comment says 'any other (the Hound's) flies zero axes as before'); tactical/duel.ts:L32 (`inputs[i]!.helm ? inputs[i]!.axes : NO_AXES`); situationModel.ts:L109 and runtime.ts:L322 (both return NO_AXES for an unattended non-Valkyrn Helm).
findings.why: Implementer A keeps today's branch. A pilot who stands up then gets an instant cut of the main thrust and no held-heading turn, so the 'returns to 0 over 30 ticks' ramp is invisible. Implementer B adds a newtonianHelm unattended branch that thrusts down the ramp, turns onto the held heading and may spend boost gas. That gives different trajectories and goldens, and the drawn path and sentAxes disagree with whichever the sim does.
findings.fix: State the rule for an unattended crew Helm in §3 and §7's step order. Recommended: for a newtonianHelm class with no attendant, the step sets crew.helm = true and flies `{ turn: running && holdHeading >= 0 ? headingTurn(...) : 0, turnBoost: helmBoost(d, NO_HELD), thrust: crewThrust(thrMille), rcsX: 0, rcsY: 0 }`. Apply the same rule in situationModel.stateAxes (L109) and runtime.ts sentAxes (L322), and add an §8 test that a crew ship whose Helm stands at thrMille 1000 thrusts down the 30-tick return and turns onto its held heading. Otherwise, keep NO_AXES and delete 'A held heading still turns it' and the returning-thrust claim.

findings.title: HELM_BARS as a createDuel option, helmVent and helmPower aren't fitted to the module contract or the rematch
findings.claim: §5 and §8 take HELM_BARS 'from the duel's options (createDuel)', but createDuel takes positional arguments and has no options object. startRound rebuilds the next round with createDuel and passes only the layout, seed, helm player, crew and class, so a test's HELM_BARS reverts to 4 at the rematch. The spec calls HELM_BARS 'not state' and d.helmVent 'unsnapshotted', but tests/duelModules.test.ts fails on any DuelState member that isn't a field or listed in DUEL_NOT_SNAPSHOTTED. The helm module's `commands` (['throttle','heading']) and `reasons` lists must also gain helmPower and 'unavailable'. A test pins the full kind list.
findings.evidence: spec L216, L300, L174-L175, L326, L121, L230-L231; state.ts:L84 (`createDuel(layout, seed, helmPlayer = 0, crew = DUEL_CREW_MIN, cls?)`); step.ts:L125 (startRound's createDuel call); modules.ts:L59-L65 (helm module commands/reasons), L92 (DUEL_NOT_SNAPSHOTTED); tests/duelModules.test.ts:L68-L70, L150-L151.
findings.why: A subagent adding these will hit failing module-contract tests or guess a createDuel signature. A HELM_BARS that is lost on the rematch makes a round-2 test silently run at 4 bars.
findings.fix: Name the interface: a sixth createDuel parameter (or an `opts: { helmBars?: number }` object) stored as `d.helmBars`. startRound passes `d.helmBars` through. List `helmBars` and `helmVent` in DUEL_NOT_SNAPSHOTTED with their reasons. Add 'helmPower' to helmModule.commands and 'unavailable' to its reasons, and update the duelModules.test.ts L150 list. For the online authority and client, state that both use the default.

findings.title: The auto-face boost band isn't wider than the boosted step, and the settle test names the wrong function
findings.claim: §4a says 'far' is 'outside a band wider than the boosted step'. But sin 5° is 5 × 256/360 ≈ 3.556 index units, the same as the boosted step (2 × 1.778), and with headingAcc carried a boosted tick can step 4 whole indices. So a boosted auto-face can step up to about 0.44 index past the target. That lands inside AUTO_FACE_SIN's ±1.78 band, so the nose doesn't chatter, but the stated rule is wrong. §8's settle test checks '`aimTurn` returns 0 for 10 straight ticks' for the held heading and auto-face too, but those go through headingTurn and autoFaceTurn.
findings.evidence: spec L197-L201, L357-L358; tuning.ts:L127 (AUTO_FACE_SIN = sin 2.5°); hunter.ts:L41-L46; step.ts:L112-L115.
findings.why: It's a small inconsistency, but a subagent may write the test against aimTurn for every case, or 'fix' the band to match the text.
findings.fix: Use BOOST_FACE_SIN = sin 6° (≈4.27 indices > 4), or reword the rule to 'any overshoot stays inside AUTO_FACE_SIN'. Phrase the test as 'helmTurn returns 0 for 10 straight ticks'.
